definitions.explanation: Formal recognition or approval by an authority, organization, or institution. Often used for officially sanctioned candidates, certified products, or publicly acknowledged relationships.

examples.japanese: {公認|こうにん}{会計士|かいけいし}になる。
{党|とう}の{公認|こうにん}{候補|こうほ}として{選挙|せんきょ}に{出|で}る。
examples.english: Run in the election as the party's officially endorsed candidate.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}らの{交際|こうさい}は{職場|しょくば}で{公認|こうにん}されている。
examples.english: Their relationship is openly acknowledged at their workplace.

notes:
Used for official endorsement or certification by organizations. Also used more casually to mean something is openly known and accepted.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{公認|こうにん}{会計士|かいけいし} (certified public accountant, CPA)
・{公認|こうにん}{候補|こうほ} (officially endorsed candidate)
・{公認|こうにん}を{得|え}る (obtain official approval)
・{公認|こうにん}される (be officially recognized)

In casual contexts, {公認|こうにん} can describe situations that are openly acknowledged even without formal certification, such as a couple whose relationship is known and accepted by those around them.
